meta.title: Top 100 Fitness Influencers 2026
meta.subtitle: The world's most influential people in fitness — ranked. Athletes, coaches, educators, and the megastars who move training culture.

scoreModel.name: Fitness Influence Score
scoreModel.gate: Two tiers. Core — fitness is their main output. Amplifiers — fitness is not their core topic, but their reach moves the whole culture when they train, transform, or talk protocols; amplifier scores carry a 0.9 relevance discount.
scoreModel.notes: Reach is log-scaled and platform-weighted (Instagram, YouTube, TikTok full weight; X half) and recomputed from researched follower counts. The five judgment factors are calibrated across research segments so no category is scored on an easier curve. Follower counts marked verified were browser-checked at the listed date; the rest are approximate.

meta.disclaimer: Follower counts are approximate (2026) and the ranking is reviewed monthly. Educational and editorial — inclusion is not an endorsement, and scores measure influence, not advice quality.

entries.name: Chris Bumstead
entries.who: Five-time Classic Physique Mr. Olympia champion, retired from competition in 2024.
entries.why: Defined the modern classic physique look and built a business empire (RAW Nutrition, Bum Energy, CBum Fitness) that outgrew the sport itself.
entries.takeaway: Treat your sport as the foundation for a business, not the ceiling on your income.

entries.name: David Goggins
entries.who: Retired Navy SEAL, ultra-endurance racer, and author of Can't Hurt Me.
entries.why: Built the modern mental-toughness genre; his callouses-and-suffering ethos is imitated across every fitness niche.
entries.takeaway: Schedule one hard thing a day you would rather skip — consistency under discomfort is the whole method.

entries.name: Kayla Itsines
entries.who: Australian trainer, co-founder of the Bikini Body Guide (BBG) and the Sweat app.
entries.why: BBG and Sweat defined the at-home women's fitness-app category and built a nine-figure business.
entries.takeaway: Package your training into a simple, repeatable program others can follow without you in the room.

entries.name: Jeff Nippard
entries.who: Natural bodybuilder and YouTuber who turns exercise-science studies into structured hypertrophy and strength programs.
entries.why: The reference standard for evidence-based lifting content; his myth-busting videos and programs set the tone the whole segment is measured against.
entries.takeaway: Before adopting any training trend, ask what the studies actually measured — copy the habit of checking sources.

entries.name: Tia-Clair Toomey
entries.who: Most decorated athlete in CrossFit Games history, 8-time Fittest Woman on Earth through the 2025 season.
entries.why: Sets the competitive standard the entire women's field trains against; her app and gear line extend that authority into commerce.
entries.takeaway: Train against the toughest standard you can find, then build products that extend your expertise past competition.

entries.name: Jeff Cavaliere
entries.who: Physical therapist and former MLB strength coach behind ATHLEAN-X, the largest science-based training channel on YouTube.
entries.why: 14M+ YouTube subscribers make him the biggest single reach in this segment; his corrective-training, fix-your-form format is widely copied.
entries.takeaway: Diagnose the root cause of an ache before treating the symptom — fix form, not just discomfort.

entries.name: Rich Froning
entries.who: Four-time individual CrossFit Games champion and multi-time team champion, founder of CrossFit Mayhem.
entries.why: Built the sport's biggest affiliate-and-media brand and still competes and coaches team events, bridging the sport's early and current eras.
entries.takeaway: Keep coaching and competing at the same time — staying hands-on keeps your teaching credible.

entries.name: Dr. Mike Israetel
entries.who: Sport scientist and co-founder of Renaissance Periodization (RP), known for periodization science and blunt on-camera debates.
entries.why: RP's app and templates put periodization science in front of a mass audience; his channel and clips generate outsized engagement and debate.
entries.takeaway: Base your training on periodization principles, not gut feel, and be ready to explain the reasoning.

entries.name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
entries.who: Seven-time Mr. Olympia, actor, former California governor, still runs the Arnold Sports Festival and a daily fitness newsletter.
entries.why: Amplifier: fitness is a fraction of his output, but his Pump Club newsletter and Arnold Classic events move the whole industry when he speaks.
entries.takeaway: Send a short, consistent update to your audience — a simple habit like a newsletter can move an industry.

entries.name: Mat Fraser
entries.who: Five-time CrossFit Games champion (2016-2020), widely regarded as the greatest individual competitor in the sport's history.
entries.why: Retired unbeaten in Games finals; his name still headlines comeback speculation and his training company keeps his standards visible.
entries.takeaway: Set a standard so high your name still defines the bar years after you stop competing.

entries.name: Cassey Ho
entries.who: Founder of Blogilates and the POPFLEX activewear brand, pioneer of Pop Pilates.
entries.why: One of the longest-running fitness YouTubers; built Pop Pilates into a format and POPFLEX into a real apparel brand.
entries.takeaway: Turn a workout format you invented into a real brand — don't just post routines, own the category.

entries.name: Mind Pump
entries.who: Three-host fitness media company (Sal Di Stefano, Adam Schafer, Justin Andrews) behind the 'Raw Fitness Truth' podcast and MAPS training programs.
entries.why: The longest-running mainstream fitness podcast, with a large, loyal, purchase-ready audience and a real coaching-programs business behind it.
entries.takeaway: Build an audience that trusts you enough to buy your program, not just watch your content.

entries.name: Ronnie Coleman
entries.who: Eight-time Mr. Olympia (1998-2005), widely regarded as one of the greatest bodybuilders ever.
entries.why: His 'Yeah buddy, lightweight' persona and record-setting Olympia run still define the sport's golden era in pop culture.
entries.takeaway: Bring real enthusiasm to hard training — a memorable attitude toward struggle outlasts the numbers you put up.

entries.name: Chris Heria
entries.who: Calisthenics athlete and founder of THENX, one of the largest bodyweight-training brands online.
entries.why: Defined the mainstream calisthenics/street-workout era and built an app-and-apparel business off it.
entries.takeaway: Master bodyweight basics before adding equipment — a strong foundation can carry an entire training business.

entries.name: Eliud Kipchoge
entries.who: Two-time Olympic marathon champion and former marathon world-record holder, first to run a sub-two-hour marathon (unofficial).
entries.why: Defined an era of distance running; his training and mindset are studied and imitated worldwide.
entries.takeaway: Study how the best distance runners structure training and mindset, then copy the discipline, not just the mileage.

entries.name: Kilian Jornet
entries.who: Mountain and skyrunning legend; holder of multiple speed records including Everest without supplemental oxygen.
entries.why: The most decorated mountain-endurance athlete alive, and co-founder of the NNormal footwear brand.
entries.takeaway: Pair endurance ambition with real specificity — train on the exact terrain and conditions you compete in.

entries.name: Joe Rogan
entries.who: Podcast host and BJJ black belt whose show constantly pulls fitness, strength, and longevity topics into mainstream conversation.
entries.why: The Joe Rogan Experience is the biggest amplification engine in health/fitness media; a single episode can send a coach, diet, or supplement viral overnight.
entries.takeaway: Check a claim before repeating it to your audience — careless amplification spreads bad advice fast.

entries.name: Jeremy Ethier
entries.who: Canadian kinesiologist-turned-YouTuber known for science-based lifting and training critique content.
entries.why: Helped mainstream the 'science-based' fitness content wave, with a real 7-8 figure coaching program behind it.
entries.takeaway: Turn credible, evidence-based content into an actual coaching product, not just more videos.

entries.name: Joe Wicks
entries.who: The Body Coach, UK home-fitness personality who ran nationwide live PE lessons during the pandemic.
entries.why: Turned a nation's living rooms into a gym class; still runs a paid app and bestselling cookbooks on the back of that trust.
entries.takeaway: Make training free and accessible first — build trust before you ever ask for payment.

entries.name: Caroline Girvan
entries.who: Irish trainer behind the EPIC and Hero dumbbell-workout programs on YouTube.
entries.why: Currently the most imitated name in home strength training; her programs drive huge, sustained view spikes.
entries.takeaway: Publish full structured programs, not single workouts — people commit harder to a plan than a routine.

entries.name: Larry Wheels
entries.who: Powerlifter, strongman, and arm-wrestler who documents extreme-strength feats and PED-assisted training openly.
entries.why: Bridges powerlifting, strongman, and bodybuilding audiences with genuine elite-level lifting numbers.
entries.takeaway: Be transparent about what actually goes into your results — honesty builds more trust than mystery.

entries.name: Eddie Hall
entries.who: 2017 World's Strongest Man and former deadlift world record holder (500kg raw).
entries.why: Crossed strongman into mainstream media via a Netflix documentary and a headline boxing match against Hafthor Bjornsson.
entries.takeaway: Look outside your own sport for the next challenge — crossing disciplines can grow your entire audience.

entries.name: Jay Cutler
entries.who: Four-time Mr. Olympia (2006, 2007, 2009, 2010), now runs a large supplement brand and gyms.
entries.why: One of the sport's most successful post-competition business builders, still a reference name for casual fans.
entries.takeaway: Plan your business after competition while you're still competing — the transition is the real test.

entries.name: Katrin Davidsdottir
entries.who: Two-time Fittest Woman on Earth (2015, 2016) and veteran competitor still contending for the Games podium.
entries.why: A decade-plus at the top with a large, loyal following and co-founded nutrition and recovery brands.
entries.takeaway: Stay in your sport for the long game — a decade of consistency builds a following no trend can.

entries.name: Nick Bare
entries.who: Army veteran, marathoner/Ironman finisher, and founder of Bare Performance Nutrition.
entries.why: Popularized the daily-vlog 'hybrid athlete' training model that fuses marathon/triathlon work with lifting.
entries.takeaway: Document your training daily and combine disciplines — hybrid training reaches a wider audience than one lane.

entries.name: Dwayne Johnson
entries.who: Actor and former pro wrestler who posts his own gym training to the largest audience of any human on Instagram.
entries.why: His 4am gym sessions and Iron Paradise content move the culture on scale alone; backed by his own Project Rock apparel line and ZOA/Teremana drink brands.
entries.takeaway: Keep showing up to train even after you've made it — visible consistency is what people actually want to see.

entries.name: Chloe Ting
entries.who: Singapore-raised, Australia-based creator behind viral workout challenges like the '2 Week Shred'.
entries.why: Most-subscribed fitness YouTuber; her challenge-video format defined the COVID-era home-workout boom worldwide.
entries.takeaway: Give people a fixed-length challenge with a clear end date — a deadline drives follow-through better than an open plan.

entries.name: Ben Bergeron
entries.who: Founder of CompTrain and CrossFit New England, coach behind multiple individual and team Games champions.
entries.why: The sport's most influential coach: his programming and mindset content are studied and copied across affiliates worldwide.
entries.takeaway: Write down your coaching philosophy, not just your workouts — the mindset behind training is what gets copied.

entries.name: Michelle Lewin
entries.who: Venezuelan bikini-fitness competitor and one of the earliest global Instagram fitness stars.
entries.why: Helped define the bikini-fitness-model aesthetic that shaped a decade of fitness content worldwide.
entries.takeaway: Recognize when a platform is still new — showing up early can define a whole category for years.

entries.name: Anllela Sagra
entries.who: Colombian fitness model and one of the most-followed Latin American fitness figures on Instagram.
entries.why: Huge cultural reach across Latin America; a defining face of the region's fitness-model wave.
entries.takeaway: Build deeply within your own community and language before chasing a global audience.

entries.name: Eva Andressa
entries.who: Brazilian bodybuilder, gym owner and one of Brazil's most-followed fitness personalities.
entries.why: Real competitive bodybuilding background plus a gym and supplement business, huge domestic cultural reach.
entries.takeaway: Back your content with a real competitive record and a real business — credibility compounds over time.

entries.name: Hafthor Bjornsson
entries.who: 2018 World's Strongest Man, former deadlift world record holder, and Game of Thrones' 'The Mountain'.
entries.why: One of the few strength athletes with genuine Hollywood crossover, plus a headline pivot into pro boxing.
entries.takeaway: Let one dramatic achievement open the door to a completely different arena — use your peak moment.

entries.name: Derek (More Plates More Dates)
entries.who: Researcher-creator focused on PED harm reduction, hormone science, and bodybuilding history.
entries.why: Shaped mainstream harm-reduction discourse around PED use and co-founded a real hormone-testing business.
entries.takeaway: Talk openly about the real risks of what you do — honest harm-reduction beats silence for building trust.

entries.name: Ramon Dino (Ramon Rocha Queiroz)
entries.who: First Brazilian man to win a Mr. Olympia title, taking the 2025 Classic Physique crown.
entries.why: Brought huge Brazilian and Latin American audiences into competitive bodybuilding's spotlight.
entries.takeaway: Represent your home country and community proudly — local pride can carry you onto a world stage.

entries.name: Layne Norton
entries.who: PhD in nutritional sciences, pro natural bodybuilder and powerlifter, runs Bio Layne coaching and the Carbon Diet Coach app.
entries.why: One of the most credentialed nutrition scientists in fitness media; rigorous myth-debunking backed by a competitive record and a PhD.
entries.takeaway: Pair your credentials with real competitive results — expertise lands harder when you've actually done the thing.

entries.name: Peter Attia
entries.who: Physician focused on longevity medicine and host of The Drive podcast, a strong advocate for strength and VO2 max training as lifespan medicine.
entries.why: Popularized the idea of training for a 'Centenarian Decathlon' among a mainstream, affluent audience, pulling fitness science into longevity media.
entries.takeaway: Train for the decades ahead, not just this season — frame fitness as a long-term investment.

entries.name: Whitney Simmons
entries.who: US lifting and glute-training creator, equity partner in the Alphalete apparel brand.
entries.why: Popularized the modern 'gym girlie' lifting-vlog format that a generation of lifters now copies.
entries.takeaway: Film your actual training honestly — a relatable, unpolished lifting vlog can become the format others copy.

entries.name: Hunter McIntyre
entries.who: Three-time HYROX World Champion and founder of BLDR Sports, formerly a top obstacle-course/Spartan racer.
entries.why: The loudest, most recognizable face driving HYROX's US growth, with a hybrid-training persona built for virality.
entries.takeaway: Get loud and visible for a new sport early — genuine enthusiasm can make you its defining face.

entries.name: Courtney Dauwalter
entries.who: Dominant ultramarathon runner; winner of UTMB, Western States, and Hardrock 100 in a single season.
entries.why: The defining ultrarunner of her generation; a Netflix documentary and repeated record-breaking wins gave the sport mainstream visibility.
entries.takeaway: Keep showing up and winning quietly — sustained results eventually earn mainstream attention on their own.

entries.name: Chris Hemsworth
entries.who: Actor and founder of Centr, a training-and-nutrition app built on his own Thor-era fitness regimens.
entries.why: Turned superhero body-prep into a subscription business millions of people actually train inside, not just watch.
entries.reach: IG 58M (verified 2026-08, Instagram profile); Centr subscribers in the millions
entries.takeaway: Turn your own training routine into something people can actually follow, not just something they admire.

entries.name: Andrew Huberman
entries.who: Stanford neuroscientist and host of the Huberman Lab podcast, with recurring episodes on resistance training, recovery and VO2 max protocols.
entries.why: His training and recovery protocol episodes move millions to change their routines overnight, the exact amplifier effect this segment is built to capture.
entries.takeaway: Explain the mechanism behind a protocol, not just the protocol — understanding why helps people actually stick with it.

entries.name: Krissy Cela
entries.who: UK trainer and co-founder of the Tone & Sculpt / EvolveYou training app.
entries.why: Built one of the UK's biggest fitness-app businesses and remains a leading voice in gym-based training for women.
entries.reach: IG 3M plus large app user base (verified IG 2026-08)
entries.takeaway: Build a structured app around your training style — a real product outlasts a following alone.

entries.name: Natacha Oceane
entries.who: French physicist turned science-based fitness YouTuber, based in the UK.
entries.why: Brings genuine scientific rigor to training and nutrition content, respected by the evidence-based fitness crowd.
entries.takeaway: Bring real technical rigor to fitness claims — earning respect from a skeptical crowd beats quick reach.

entries.name: Dorian Yates
entries.who: Six-time Mr. Olympia (1992-1997), credited with starting bodybuilding's 'mass monster' era.
entries.why: His high-intensity training template still shapes how top-level bodybuilders train decades later.
entries.takeaway: Design a training method precise enough that people are still following it decades later.

entries.name: Cameron Hanes
entries.who: Bowhunter and ultra-distance runner known for the 'Keep Hammering' philosophy.
entries.why: Fused extreme endurance running with hunting culture; frequent Joe Rogan crossover gave the ethos mainstream reach.
entries.takeaway: Combine two personal passions into one identity — a distinct crossover niche expands your reach and your mission.

entries.name: Rich Roll
entries.who: Plant-based ultra-endurance athlete (Ultraman finisher) and host of The Rich Roll Podcast.
entries.why: Defined the plant-based endurance/wellness podcast genre; his platform shapes mainstream health and fitness discourse.
entries.takeaway: Turn your own comeback story into a long-form platform — personal transformation content builds lasting trust.

entries.name: Knees Over Toes Guy
entries.who: Ben Patrick, former basketball player turned knee-rehab specialist, creator of the ATG (Athletic Truth Group) training system.
entries.why: Reframed how lifters and rehab clients think about knee health; the ATG split squat became a global gym staple in a few years.
entries.takeaway: Question standard advice about an injury-prone area — a fresh rehab approach can become a global habit.

entries.name: Sam Sulek
entries.who: College-age gym creator turned the biggest name in raw workout-vlog content since 2023.
entries.why: Set off a wave of copycat long-form training vlogs; his views routinely outstrip his subscriber count.
entries.takeaway: Post your actual training honestly and often — raw, unpolished footage can outperform produced content.

entries.name: Annie Thorisdottir
entries.who: First two-time Fittest Woman on Earth (2011, 2012), one of the sport's founding stars.
entries.why: Her early dominance helped put women's CrossFit on equal billing with the men's field; still a respected voice and occasional competitor.
entries.takeaway: Compete early and well in a young sport — your results help define the field for everyone after.

entries.name: Magnus Midtbø
entries.who: Norwegian rock climber whose channel regularly features strength, bodybuilding, and endurance training challenges.
entries.why: Bridges climbing and general fitness content with viral training-challenge videos and a growing gear brand.
entries.takeaway: Bring outsiders from your own niche into mainstream fitness challenges — crossover content grows both audiences.

entries.name: Lilly Sabri
entries.who: UK physiotherapist and trainer focused on pilates, pelvic floor and postpartum fitness.
entries.why: Brings a clinical, physiotherapy-backed angle to a niche most fitness creators ignore, with a loyal community.
entries.takeaway: Address pelvic floor and postpartum recovery directly — clinical rehab work belongs in training plans, not just aesthetics.

entries.name: Mike O'Hearn
entries.who: Veteran natural bodybuilder, model, and actor known as 'The Maniac' or 'The Titan'.
entries.why: Over 30 years of visible relevance across bodybuilding, TV, and film work, longer than almost anyone in the segment.
entries.takeaway: Play the long game — build a training identity that stays visible for decades, not one season.

entries.name: MadFit (Maddie Lymburner)
entries.who: Canadian creator behind MadFit, one of the largest no-equipment, low-noise home-workout channels on YouTube.
entries.why: Defined the quiet, apartment-friendly home workout format that exploded during the pandemic and never really faded.
entries.takeaway: Keep home workouts quiet and equipment-free — removing noise and gear barriers grows a bigger audience.

entries.name: Squat University
entries.who: Aaron Horschig, physical therapist and strength coach, built Squat University on lift-specific biomechanics and injury-prevention content.
entries.why: The go-to reference for lifters diagnosing pain and technique flaws; his format has been widely copied by other PT-creators.
entries.takeaway: Diagnose your own lifting pain before pushing through it — treat technique flaws as injury prevention.

entries.name: Justin Medeiros
entries.who: Two-time Fittest Man on Earth (2021, 2022) and one of the most consistently ranked men of the past five years.
entries.why: A crossover face for the sport with strong brand deals and steady top-5 Games finishes since his titles.
entries.takeaway: Chase consistent top finishes over one big peak — steady placing builds a longer career than a single win.

entries.name: Marcus Filly
entries.who: Former CrossFit Games competitor turned founder of Functional Bodybuilding, a training style he popularized.
entries.why: Created and named a training category now used across gyms worldwide, backed by a real subscription-program business.
entries.takeaway: Name your training style and build a real program around it, not just a highlight reel.

entries.name: Ross Edgley
entries.who: Extreme-endurance athlete holding multiple Guinness World Records, including swimming around Great Britain.
entries.why: Mainstream crossover endurance figure (bestselling author, frequent podcast guest) who legitimizes extreme feats scientifically.
entries.takeaway: Back extreme feats with real documentation and science — credibility comes from proof, not the stunt alone.

entries.name: Pamela Reif
entries.who: German home-workout and dance-fitness creator, one of Europe's biggest fitness YouTubers.
entries.why: Defined the free, no-equipment home-workout genre in Europe and stayed dominant for a decade.
entries.takeaway: Keep workouts free and equipment-free — remove every barrier between someone and their first rep.

entries.name: Thomas DeLauer
entries.who: Former bodybuilder turned science communicator covering fat loss, fasting and metabolic health.
entries.why: One of the earliest YouTubers to build a channel purely on translating studies into practical diet and fasting protocols.
entries.takeaway: Translate research studies into plain, practical protocols people can actually follow.

entries.name: Greg Doucette
entries.who: IFBB pro bodybuilder and coach known for calling out fraud and misinformation in bodybuilding media.
entries.why: A rare credentialed insider voice who publicly polices claims made by other bodybuilding influencers.
entries.takeaway: Publicly fact-check claims in your niche — policing misinformation builds trust faster than hype does.

entries.name: Sondre Berg
entries.who: Founder of Nordic Strength, a large YouTube channel covering parkour, calisthenics, and freerunning.
entries.why: One of the biggest bodyweight-athletics channels globally, sustaining strong output for years.
entries.takeaway: Commit to one bodyweight discipline and post consistently for years — longevity beats a single viral clip.

entries.name: Stan Efferding
entries.who: Pro bodybuilder and powerlifter, creator of the Vertical Diet, coaches elite strength and physique athletes.
entries.why: A rare crossover between an elite competitive record in two sports and real nutrition-coaching credibility.
entries.takeaway: Pair a simple, repeatable diet system with real competitive results before coaching others on it.

entries.name: Bryan Johnson
entries.who: Tech entrepreneur running the 'Don't Die' Blueprint longevity protocol on himself, publishing exhaustive personal training and biomarker data.
entries.why: The biggest voice in longevity: turned his own body into a public experiment, publishes every blood panel and biomarker, and his 'Don't Die' Netflix documentary pushed protocol culture into the mainstream.
entries.takeaway: Track and publish your own detailed biomarker data — transparency about your own body drives interest.

entries.name: Nick Walker
entries.who: Men's Open pro bodybuilder known as 'The Mutant', multiple Arnold Classic winner.
entries.why: One of the biggest mass-monster physiques currently competing, influential in the current Open bodybuilding trend.
entries.takeaway: Compete at the top level in your sport before building a following around your physique.

entries.name: Sara Sigmundsdottir
entries.who: Longtime individual Games competitor and Mayhem Freedom team athlete known for raw strength and candid, personality-driven content.
entries.why: One of the more entertaining, outspoken voices in the sport, with a following that predates and outlasts her competitive peak.
entries.takeaway: Stay candid and personality-driven on camera — an authentic voice outlasts your competitive peak.

entries.name: Mark Rippetoe
entries.who: Strength coach and author of 'Starting Strength,' the foundational modern barbell-training text.
entries.why: Nearly every other strength coach on this list cites his programming; the Starting Strength template is still the default beginner program decades on.
entries.takeaway: Write your training method down clearly enough that beginners can follow it without you.

entries.name: Kelly Starrett
entries.who: Physical therapist and mobility coach, co-founder of The Ready State (formerly MobilityWOD), author of 'Becoming a Supple Leopard.'
entries.why: Mainstreamed mobility work as a training pillar; his framework is now standard vocabulary in CrossFit and strength gyms.
entries.takeaway: Treat mobility work as a training pillar, not an afterthought before or after lifting.

entries.name: Tren Twins
entries.who: Identical twins Christian and Michael Gaiera, comedic gym-vlog duo who blew up in under two years.
entries.why: Their deadpan, self-aware 'gym bro' format got copied across the creator economy faster than almost anyone else's.
entries.takeaway: Bring humor and personality into training content — a distinct tone spreads faster than raw information.

entries.name: Bradley Martyn
entries.who: Gym-culture veteran and owner of the Zoo Culture gym chain in California.
entries.why: One of the longest-running gym-vlog creators; turned his following into an actual gym business, not just content.
entries.takeaway: Turn your following into a real business, like a gym, not just more content.

entries.name: Joey Swoll
entries.who: Former gym manager turned viral 'gym positivity' creator who calls out bullying and gym-shaming clips.
entries.why: Started an entire anti-gym-shaming content genre now copied by dozens of smaller creators.
entries.takeaway: Call out gym-shaming and bullying publicly — positivity content builds loyalty as fast as intensity does.

entries.name: Laura Horvath
entries.who: 2023 Fittest Woman on Earth, Hungary's first CrossFit Games champion.
entries.why: Broke a long US/Icelandic/Australian hold on the women's title and remains a top podium threat.
entries.takeaway: Keep contending at the top level year after year — sustained podium threat matters more than one win.

entries.name: Don Saladino
entries.who: Trainer behind the superhero physiques of Ryan Reynolds, Blake Lively, Hugh Jackman, and other Hollywood A-listers.
entries.why: One of the most trusted names in actor body-prep, with a training app and podcast extending his reach past his private clients.
entries.takeaway: Extend one-on-one coaching reach with a podcast or app so it isn't limited to private clients.

entries.name: Eugene Teo
entries.who: Natural bodybuilding coach and YouTuber known for minimalist, sustainable training templates grounded in research.
entries.why: Represents the calm, low-hype wing of evidence-based lifting, popular with viewers fatigued by extreme claims.
entries.takeaway: Favor a calm, minimalist training template over hype — sustainability beats big claims for most people.

entries.name: Greg Nuckols
entries.who: Powerlifter and researcher, co-founder of Stronger By Science, publishing deep-dive literature reviews on training and nutrition.
entries.why: The most cited 'read the papers so you don't have to' resource in the segment, shaping how other creators talk about the evidence.
entries.takeaway: Read the primary research yourself and cite it — sourced claims beat unfounded ones.

entries.name: Dr. Gabrielle Lyon
entries.who: Physician specializing in 'muscle-centric medicine,' podcast host and advocate for protein intake and resistance training as preventive medicine.
entries.why: A fast-growing crossover figure connecting clinical medicine to strength-training messaging for a mainstream health audience.
entries.takeaway: Frame resistance training and protein intake as preventive medicine, not just aesthetics.

entries.name: Grow with Jo
entries.who: UK creator behind fast-growing low-impact and walking-workout videos on YouTube.
entries.why: Popularized the walking-workout format for a broad, often older audience underserved by typical HIIT content.
entries.takeaway: Serve an underserved audience directly — low-impact workouts open training to people HIIT excludes.

entries.name: Tammy Hembrow
entries.who: Australian fitness influencer, founder of Saski Collection and the Tammy Fit training app.
entries.why: Pioneered the fitness-influencer-to-apparel-and-app-brand playbook that many others later copied.
entries.takeaway: Turn your personal following into your own apparel or app brand instead of just endorsing others'.

entries.name: David Laid
entries.who: Natural-aesthetics creator who went viral as a teenager for a dramatic physique transformation.
entries.why: One of the longest-running faces of the 'aesthetic natural' training niche, still posting after nearly a decade.
entries.takeaway: Keep showing up in the same niche for years — sheer longevity builds trust on its own.

entries.name: Alexander Roncevic
entries.who: Austrian HYROX World Champion and double world-record holder, first athlete to break the 52-minute barrier.
entries.why: The technical benchmark of the sport right now, setting times and standards other elite racers chase.
entries.takeaway: Set a measurable technical benchmark in your discipline that others have to chase.

entries.name: FitnessFAQs (Daniel Vadnal)
entries.who: Weighted-calisthenics coach and YouTuber teaching skill progressions (muscle-up, front lever, planche).
entries.why: Respected technical authority in the calisthenics coaching niche with a decade of steady, credible output.
entries.takeaway: Break big skills into clear step-by-step progressions and stay consistent for years.

entries.name: Jillian Michaels
entries.who: The Biggest Loser's tough-love trainer, still running her own fitness app and program business.
entries.why: Defined the 2000s-2010s reality-TV transformation genre and put certified personal training in front of a mass audience.
entries.takeaway: Bring certified, structured coaching to a mass audience instead of just motivational talk.

entries.name: Lucy Wyndham-Read
entries.who: British fitness instructor known for low-impact, no-equipment home workouts aimed at beginners and older audiences.
entries.why: Pioneered accessible workout content for a demographic most fitness media ignores, with strong international reach on YouTube.
entries.reach: YT 1.96M · IG 242K (approx 2026, from public bio stats)
entries.takeaway: Design workouts specifically for beginners and older audiences most fitness media ignores.

entries.name: Stephanie Buttermore
entries.who: US creator with a PhD in biomedical science, known for publicly documenting her own reverse-diet recovery.
entries.why: Turned her own metabolic-recovery experiment into one of the most credible physiology deep-dives in fitness media.
entries.takeaway: Document your own physiology experiment publicly — personal data builds more credibility than advice alone.

entries.name: Will Tennyson
entries.who: Scottish-Canadian fitness YouTuber known for 'try the diet of X celebrity' and coaching content.
entries.why: A steady, credentialed voice in natural bodybuilding YouTube with almost a decade of consistent output.
entries.takeaway: Turn curiosity experiments, like trying someone else's diet, into structured, credentialed content.

entries.name: Jeffrey Adler
entries.who: 2023 Fittest Man on Earth and back-to-back Rogue Invitational champion (2024, 2025).
entries.why: Canada's most decorated current male competitor, still adding to a growing trophy case.
entries.takeaway: Keep adding wins year after year — a growing record speaks louder than a single title.

entries.name: Brooke Wells
entries.who: Longtime individual Games competitor and one of the most consistent top-10 women of the past decade.
entries.why: A steady top finisher with strong sponsor relationships and a loyal training-content following.
entries.takeaway: Build sponsor relationships around consistent top finishes, not just one standout result.

entries.name: Marston Sawyers
entries.who: Co-founder of the Buttery Bros, CrossFit's best-known documentary and comedy media duo (with Heber Cannon).
entries.why: Their films and event coverage have shaped how the whole sport is presented on camera, and their apparel brand extends that reach.
entries.takeaway: Document your sport on camera with real production value — how it's filmed shapes how it's seen.

entries.name: Craig Richey
entries.who: British Weightlifting national champion turned YouTube fitness personality, known for daily follow-along cardio and CrossFit-style content.
entries.why: One of the sport's longest-running creators, translating CrossFit and weightlifting training into daily content for a mainstream audience.
entries.takeaway: Translate elite-level training into daily, follow-along content a mainstream audience can actually do.

entries.name: Wim Hof
entries.who: Dutch extreme athlete known as 'The Iceman' for cold-exposure and breathing-method world records.
entries.why: Fitness is not his core topic, but his cold-exposure and breathwork method moved training culture broadly and built a large certified-instructor business.
entries.takeaway: Package your method into a certification program so others can teach it too.

entries.name: Terry Crews
entries.who: Actor and former NFL player known for a decades-long, visibly maintained bodybuilder physique.
entries.why: Mainstream TV and film presence keeps an old-school bodybuilding aesthetic in front of a general audience that would never watch a bodybuilding channel.
entries.takeaway: Maintain a visible physique consistently across decades, not just for a single role or season.

entries.name: Harley Pasternak
entries.who: Canadian celebrity trainer and nutritionist with an MSc in exercise physiology, longtime trainer to pop stars and reality-TV names.
entries.why: Regular mainstream media go-to on nutrition and exercise, with the 5-Factor Diet a genuine bestseller-era phenomenon.
entries.takeaway: Pair a real science credential with mainstream media appearances to reach beyond your own following.

entries.name: growingannanas (Anna Engelschall)
entries.who: Austrian creator known for glute-focused home and gym programs and a large 'Team Grow' community.
entries.why: Mainstreamed the glute-training niche into a broad international audience with a real program business behind it.
entries.takeaway: Build a real community, not just followers, around one focused training niche.

entries.name: Menno Henselmans
entries.who: Evidence-based personal trainer and researcher who runs Bayesian Bodybuilding and regularly critiques published hypertrophy studies.
entries.why: Among the most technically respected voices in evidence-based coaching, cited by peer coaches more than by mass audience size.
entries.takeaway: Critique published research directly — respect from peer coaches matters as much as audience size.

entries.name: Meg Squats
entries.who: Meg Gallagher, competitive powerlifter and coach, YouTuber covering training logs, form checks and women's strength content.
entries.why: One of the most visible women in barbell-strength media, credited with helping grow the female powerlifting audience.
entries.takeaway: Post your own training logs and form checks openly to grow your niche's audience.

entries.name: Sydney Cummings
entries.who: US trainer known for free, daily-cadence YouTube strength workouts.
entries.why: Sustained a consistent daily-upload gym-workout channel for years, building strong community loyalty.
entries.takeaway: Show up daily with free workouts — consistent cadence builds community loyalty over any single video.

entries.name: Heather Robertson
entries.who: Canadian trainer known for free no-equipment and dumbbell workout videos on YouTube.
entries.why: Long-running, reliable source for structured home-workout programming with a loyal following.
entries.takeaway: Be the reliable, no-equipment option people return to — reliability outlasts flashier competitors.

entries.name: Alex Eubank
entries.who: Aesthetics-focused creator known for full-day-of-eating and cutting/bulking vlogs.
entries.why: Popularized the modern 'lean bulk' aesthetic content format now standard across natural bodybuilding YouTube.
entries.takeaway: Document your full day of eating alongside training — food transparency builds trust as much as workouts do.

entries.name: Jesse James West
entries.who: Comedic gym-collaboration creator who films workouts with other influencers and pro athletes.
entries.why: Pioneered the collab-heavy comedic gym-vlog format that many mid-tier creators now run on.
entries.takeaway: Collaborate with other creators and athletes on camera — shared audiences grow faster than solo content.

entries.name: James Sprague
entries.who: Two-time Fittest Man on Earth (2024, 2026), the current standard-bearer of the men's field.
entries.why: Fresh off defending his title, he is the sport's newest breakout star, with reach still catching up to his results.
entries.takeaway: Let results speak first — reach and recognition can catch up to real achievement later.

entries.name: Noah Ohlsen
entries.who: Ten-plus-year individual Games competitor, among the most durable men's careers in the sport.
entries.why: Rarely misses a Games appearance and is respected as one of the field's most consistent performers.
entries.takeaway: Show up every year without fail — durability earns respect that single peak performances don't.

bubblingUnder.name: Lazar Novović
bubblingUnder.who: Serbian calisthenics athlete known for extreme strength feats like weighted one-arm pull-ups.
bubblingUnder.why: Viral demonstrations of raw bodyweight strength keep the calisthenics discipline visible internationally.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Demonstrate one extreme, verifiable strength feat — a single striking clip can carry a whole discipline.

bubblingUnder.name: Mark Wahlberg
bubblingUnder.who: Actor and entrepreneur whose 2:30am-wake-up training routine became a recurring media story.
bubblingUnder.why: Backs it with real businesses: Municipal performance apparel and a significant stake in the F45 gym franchise chain.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Back a highly visible routine, like an early wake-up habit, with real business investment, not just talk.

bubblingUnder.name: Fraser Wilson
bubblingUnder.who: Australian YouTuber known for viral home ab and core-focused workout videos.
bubblingUnder.why: Helped popularize the short, no-equipment home-workout video format that later dominated fitness YouTube and Shorts.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Make workout videos short and equipment-free — brevity spreads further than long-form content.

bubblingUnder.name: Alan Thrall
bubblingUnder.who: Powerlifting gym owner and coach (Untamed Strength) known for barbell-technique breakdowns and gym-culture commentary.
bubblingUnder.why: A bridge between old-school strength coaching and modern YouTube fitness media, respected in both worlds.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Bridge old-school gym coaching with modern video breakdowns of barbell technique.

bubblingUnder.name: Hanna Oberg
bubblingUnder.who: Swedish fitness influencer, nutrition advisor and founder of the Ownu training app.
bubblingUnder.why: One of the Nordic region's biggest fitness voices, with a real app business behind the following.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Turn nutrition advice and a following into your own training app, not just sponsored content.

bubblingUnder.name: Robin Gallant
bubblingUnder.who: Canadian trainer with a biochemistry degree and NSCA-CSCS certification, known for science-based glute training.
bubblingUnder.why: Smaller reach than most on this list but genuinely credentialed, explaining muscle mechanics most creators skip.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Explain the actual muscle mechanics behind an exercise instead of just demonstrating it.

bubblingUnder.name: Aimee Cringle
bubblingUnder.who: 2026 Fittest Woman on Earth, the first British Games champion since Sam Briggs in 2013.
bubblingUnder.why: A six-year rise from mid-pack to champion that is reshaping the UK CrossFit scene and drawing new mainstream press.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Trust a slow multi-year rise — years of incremental progress can still end in a title.

bubblingUnder.name: Emi Wong
bubblingUnder.who: Hong Kong-based fitness and lifestyle YouTuber, bilingual (English/Cantonese) creator.
bubblingUnder.why: One of the most-recognized fitness voices across Asian markets, with strong crossover into China.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Create content in more than one language to reach markets other creators overlook.

bubblingUnder.name: Urs Kalecinski
bubblingUnder.who: 2023 Classic Physique Mr. Olympia champion from Germany.
bubblingUnder.why: The rising European face of classic physique now that Bumstead has stepped back from competing.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Step into the gap left by a retiring champion — there is room for a new face in every category.

bubblingUnder.name: Zach Bitter
bubblingUnder.who: Ultrarunning world-record holder (100-mile) and endurance coach/podcaster.
bubblingUnder.why: Elite competitive record plus a coaching and podcast platform that shapes ultrarunning training discourse.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Pair a genuine competitive record with coaching and a podcast to shape how your sport is discussed.

bubblingUnder.name: Amelia Boone
bubblingUnder.who: Corporate attorney turned elite obstacle-course-racing champion, multiple World's Toughest Mudder titles.
bubblingUnder.why: Helped legitimize OCR as a competitive endurance sport with an elite record and outspoken advocacy for women in endurance.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Use your platform to advocate publicly for underrepresented groups in your sport, not just compete.

bubblingUnder.name: Tracy Anderson
bubblingUnder.who: Celebrity trainer behind the dance-cardio Tracy Anderson Method, longtime trainer to Gwyneth Paltrow and other A-listers.
bubblingUnder.why: Built a lasting studio-and-streaming business around a signature technique widely imitated across the celebrity-trainer space.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Name your own training method and build both a studio and a streaming product around it.

bubblingUnder.name: Rhonda Patrick
bubblingUnder.who: Biomedical scientist and host of FoundMyFitness, covering nutrition, exercise physiology and longevity research in technical depth.
bubblingUnder.why: Trusted by both hardcore researchers and mainstream health podcasters for accurate deep dives that regularly feature exercise-science protocols.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Go deep on technical detail — accuracy earns trust from experts and mainstream audiences at once.

bubblingUnder.name: Sommer Ray
bubblingUnder.who: US fitness model and social-media star who broke out through glute-training content.
bubblingUnder.why: One of the biggest fitness-model accounts of the late 2010s; still huge reach though now more general influencer content.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: A focused early niche can carry your reach even after your content broadens later.

bubblingUnder.name: Senada Greca
bubblingUnder.who: Albanian-American gym-training creator and fitness model with a large Instagram following.
bubblingUnder.why: Prominent in the gym-influencer wave that pushed women's strength training into mainstream social feeds.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Post real gym-training content, not just posed shots — it helps make strength training mainstream.

bubblingUnder.name: Alexia Clark
bubblingUnder.who: US creator known as the 'Queen of Workouts', posting widely reposted gym total-body routines.
bubblingUnder.why: Her workout-clip format became a template widely copied across fitness social media.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Design a repeatable workout-clip format simple enough that others end up copying it.

bubblingUnder.name: Kristi Eramo O'Connell
bubblingUnder.who: Multiple-time individual Games competitor and coach known for technical lifting content.
bubblingUnder.why: A steady presence bridging elite competition and everyday training advice for a broad training audience.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Translate elite competition experience into training advice an everyday lifter can actually use.

bubblingUnder.name: Lauren Weeks
bubblingUnder.who: Three-time HYROX World Champion, the most decorated woman in the sport.
bubblingUnder.why: The benchmark competitor for women's HYROX as the sport professionalizes and its audience grows.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Set the technical benchmark in a growing sport early — being first-best compounds as the sport grows.

bubblingUnder.name: Alec Blenis
bubblingUnder.who: DEKA Fit hybrid-fitness competitor and coach.
bubblingUnder.why: Competitive record in hybrid/functional racing gives him credibility as the format's growth continues.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Earn credibility through actual competitive results in your discipline before building a coaching brand.

bubblingUnder.name: Frank Medrano
bubblingUnder.who: Early viral calisthenics figure known for planche and human-flag feats.
bubblingUnder.why: Helped launch the global calisthenics movement in the early 2010s, though output has slowed in recent years.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Launching a movement matters, but staying consistent afterward is what keeps you relevant.

bubblingUnder.name: Magnus Lygdback
bubblingUnder.who: Swedish trainer behind Chris Hemsworth's Thor transformation and prep for Ben Affleck, Alicia Vikander, and other stars.
bubblingUnder.why: The Magnus Method turned superhero-prep training into a widely referenced methodology and app.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Package a celebrity-training methodology into a named system and an app anyone can access.

bubblingUnder.name: Shaun T
bubblingUnder.who: Dance-fitness trainer behind Beachbody's Insanity and T25 programs, a defining wave of 2010s home HIIT.
bubblingUnder.why: His DVD-and-streaming programs shaped a decade of home HIIT culture, even as Beachbody's own decline has cooled his current reach.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Don't let your reach depend entirely on one platform or distributor's success.

bubblingUnder.name: Gunnar Peterson
bubblingUnder.who: Longtime celebrity and NBA-adjacent strength trainer, known for training the Kardashian-Jenner family and pro athletes.
bubblingUnder.why: 25+ years of elite client results and constant mainstream media presence, even without a mass personal following of his own.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Elite client results and media presence can build a career even without a huge personal following.

bubblingUnder.name: Denise Austin
bubblingUnder.who: Pioneer of daytime-TV home fitness in the 1980s-90s, still active in fitness media today.
bubblingUnder.why: Foundational figure for the entire home-workout-video genre that every later creator on this list is descended from.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Stay active in your field for decades — foundational figures earn respect long after the trend passes.

bubblingUnder.name: Daisy Keech
bubblingUnder.who: US fitness and lifestyle creator, founder of the Formation training app.
bubblingUnder.why: Drove the TikTok-era 'hourglass' workout trend and built a following-turned-app business around it.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Convert a viral training trend into a lasting app business before the trend fades.

bubblingUnder.name: Jen Selter
bubblingUnder.who: US creator widely credited as one of the first Instagram-era 'fitness selfie' stars.
bubblingUnder.why: Helped invent the glute-focused fitness-Instagram genre years before it became an industry standard.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Move early into a new content format — being first in a genre outlasts being biggest later.

bubblingUnder.name: Lexx Little
bubblingUnder.who: Powerlifter and bodybuilder with dwarfism who competes and trains alongside able-bodied lifters.
bubblingUnder.why: Built one of fitness's most inspirational niches by posting real training numbers, not just transformation photos.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Post your real training numbers, not just transformation photos — verifiable data builds more respect.

bubblingUnder.name: Emma Lawson
bubblingUnder.who: Runner-up at the 2026 CrossFit Games and one of the sport's most consistent young podium threats.
bubblingUnder.why: Canada's top current CrossFit export, with a fast-growing following tracking her rise toward a title.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Let people follow your rise in real time — a growing story is as compelling as a finished one.

bubblingUnder.name: Dan John
bubblingUnder.who: Veteran strength coach, author and lecturer known for simple, durable training philosophy ('Easy Strength').
bubblingUnder.why: A coach's coach: decades of influence on how other strength coaches teach and write, measured more in citations than followers.
bubblingUnder.reach: IG ~80K, wider reach via books and seminars (approx 2026)
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Aim to influence how other coaches teach, not just how many people follow you directly.

bubblingUnder.name: Dr. Stuart McGill
bubblingUnder.who: Retired professor of spine biomechanics, the most-cited researcher on low-back injury and the 'McGill Big 3' core-training protocol.
bubblingUnder.why: The scientific backbone cited by nearly every strength coach on spine safety; low social reach but outsized academic and coaching-world credibility.
bubblingUnder.reach: IG ~60K, cited across tens of thousands of academic and coaching sources (approx 2026)
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Build credibility through citations and research, not social reach — the right audience will still find you.

bubblingUnder.name: Linn Lowes
bubblingUnder.who: Swedish trainer and nutrition coach known for glute-focused gym programs (Body Temple, on the Athli app).
bubblingUnder.why: A leading Nordic voice in structured glute and strength programming, sold through her own app partnerships.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Sell structured programming through an app partnership instead of building distribution from scratch.

bubblingUnder.name: Noel Deyzel
bubblingUnder.who: South African-born giant-frame creator known for size-focused training content.
bubblingUnder.why: Rapid follower growth on sheer physical novelty, part of the current wave of size-first, competition-optional creators.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Physical novelty alone can grow a following fast, but a real competitive record adds durability.

bubblingUnder.name: Dallin Pepper
bubblingUnder.who: Multiple-time CrossFit Games podium finisher, runner-up in 2026, long tipped as the next Fittest Man on Earth.
bubblingUnder.why: A young, telegenic contender whose near-misses have made him one of the most-discussed men in the sport.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Being close to winning repeatedly can build as much attention as actually winning.

bubblingUnder.name: Colin O'Brady
bubblingUnder.who: Extreme-endurance explorer; first to complete a solo, unsupported crossing of Antarctica.
bubblingUnder.why: Verified world records in polar and mountain endurance feats, plus a speaking/media platform built on them.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Turn a verified world record into a speaking and media platform, not a one-time headline.

bubblingUnder.name: Kim French
bubblingUnder.who: NASM-certified trainer known for a documented postpartum body-transformation story and glute-focused programming.
bubblingUnder.why: One of the mainstream faces of the 'mom transformation' fitness niche, with her own app and gear brand.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Document your own transformation story honestly — it can become the foundation for an app or brand.

bubblingUnder.name: Liver King (Brian Johnson)
bubblingUnder.who: Carnivore/ancestral-lifestyle influencer built around raw-organ eating and a hyper-muscular physique.
bubblingUnder.why: At his peak drove one of the biggest fitness-adjacent brand businesses (Ancestral Supplements) and defined the carnivore-aesthetic trend before the scandal.
bubblingUnder.warning: Publicly admitted in December 2022 to extensive steroid use after previously denying it for years while marketing an all-natural 'ancestral' persona; faced consumer lawsuits over the deception.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Tell the truth about what's actually behind your results — deception catches up and destroys trust fast.

bubblingUnder.name: Danielle Brandon
bubblingUnder.who: Multiple-time CrossFit Games individual competitor known for explosive gymnastics and a fast-growing profile.
bubblingUnder.why: One of the more talked-about rising women in the sport, with viral-friendly training clips.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Showcase your most explosive, viral-friendly skill clips — standout moments travel further than full workouts.

bubblingUnder.name: Chandler Smith
bubblingUnder.who: Individual Games competitor and one of the sport's strongest young men, known for elite weightlifting numbers.
bubblingUnder.why: A rising name whose raw strength numbers get shared well outside the CrossFit community.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Share your raw strength numbers — impressive lifts travel to audiences outside your home sport.

bubblingUnder.name: Sylvester Stallone
bubblingUnder.who: Actor whose Rocky/Rambo-era physique defined 1980s action-hero fitness and who still posts gym footage in his late 70s.
bubblingUnder.why: Periodic viral gym clips ('it gets harder and harder, that's why you gotta push') keep an older audience engaged with strength training as a lifelong habit.
bubblingUnder.reach: IG approx 13-14M (approx 2026, based on 2025 profile data)
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Keep training visibly into old age — it shows strength training as a lifelong habit, not a young person's game.

bubblingUnder.name: Megan Jacoby
bubblingUnder.who: 2024 HYROX World Champion and one of the sport's top-ranked women.
bubblingUnder.why: A recent breakout champion helping legitimize HYROX as a pro women's circuit.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: A single breakout title can help legitimize an entire circuit — win publicly and the sport rises with you.

bubblingUnder.name: Ben Parkes
bubblingUnder.who: UK street-workout and calisthenics athlete/coach.
bubblingUnder.why: Regular presence in the European calisthenics scene, contributing to bodyweight-training's continued growth.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Stay a regular, visible presence in your local scene — steady contribution grows a discipline over time.

bubblingUnder.name: Regan Grimes
bubblingUnder.who: Canadian Men's Open pro bodybuilder, repeat top-5 Olympia finisher.
bubblingUnder.why: A consistent top-tier competitor representing Canada on the Olympia stage.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Be the consistent top-tier finisher year after year — reliability at the highest level builds its own following.

bubblingUnder.name: Austin Dunham
bubblingUnder.who: Fitness YouTuber known for calisthenics-to-bodybuilding transformation content.
bubblingUnder.why: Draws a large audience with progressive-overload calisthenics and physique-transformation storytelling.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Tell your progressive-overload transformation as a story, not just a set of numbers.

bubblingUnder.name: Kofuzi
bubblingUnder.who: Calisthenics YouTuber known for park-workout content and gymnastics-strength skill tutorials.
bubblingUnder.why: Long-running niche voice in the street-workout/calisthenics scene with a loyal, engaged following.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Stay in your niche and keep showing up — a smaller, loyal following beats a big, disengaged one.

bubblingUnder.name: The Ginger Runner (Ethan Newberry)
bubblingUnder.who: Trail-running YouTuber and gear reviewer, longtime voice in the ultrarunning media space.
bubblingUnder.why: Helped popularize trail/ultrarunning as YouTube content years before it went mainstream.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Cover a niche sport on video years before it goes mainstream — early coverage compounds later.

bubblingUnder.name: Fergus Crawley
bubblingUnder.who: Ultrarunner, writer, and content creator covering trail and mountain running.
bubblingUnder.why: Growing voice in the ultrarunning content space, blending competitive racing with storytelling.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Blend your competitive results with genuine storytelling — narrative makes racing content stick.

bubblingUnder.name: Jesse Itzler
bubblingUnder.who: Entrepreneur and author (Living with a SEAL) who founded the 29029 Everesting endurance-event business.
bubblingUnder.why: Fitness is secondary to his entrepreneurship, but his hybrid-mindset content and endurance events move mainstream audiences into extreme fitness challenges.
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Build an actual event business around your mindset content, not just motivational posts.
